title: Exhaustive coordinate filtration from a successor enlargement property
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $M$ an $A$-module, $I$ a set and $(Q_i)_{i\in I}$ any family of $B$-modules. Fix a $B$-linear isomorphism $\theta:B\otimes_A M\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. For $H\subseteq I$ let $D_H$ be the coordinate submodule of families vanishing outside $H$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule], and for an $A$-submodule $U\subseteq M$ put $T(U)=\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A U\to B\otimes_A M))$, using the inclusion-induced map. Assume the following successor property: for every $U\subseteq M$, $H\subseteq I$ with $T(U)=D_H$, and $x\in M\setminus U$, there exist $V\subseteq M$ and $H'\subseteq I$ with $U\subseteq V$, $x\in V$, $H\subseteq H'$, $T(V)=D_{H'}$ and $V/U$ countably generated and projective over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Here countably generated means spanned by an at most countable subset using finite linear combinations. Fix a well-order on the underlying set of $M$, with order type the set ordinal $\kappa$ and enumeration $(e_\alpha)_{\alpha<\kappa}$. Then there are increasing families $(M_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$ of $A$-submodules of $M$ and $(H_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$ of subsets of $I$, satisfying $M_0=0$, $H_0=\varnothing$, $M_\kappa=M$ and $T(M_\alpha)=D_{H_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha\leq\kappa$. For every nonzero limit ordinal $\lambda\leq\kappa$ they satisfy $M_\lambda=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}M_\alpha$ and $H_\lambda=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}H_\alpha$. For every $\alpha<\kappa$, the module $M_{\alpha+1}/M_\alpha$ is countably generated and projective. If $M_\alpha\ne M$, $M_{\alpha+1}$ contains the least element of $M\setminus M_\alpha$ in the chosen order; otherwise $M_{\alpha+1}=M_\alpha$ and $H_{\alpha+1}=H_\alpha$. In particular $e_\beta\in M_\alpha$ whenever $\beta<\alpha\leq\kappa$. Neither flatness of $A\to B$ nor countable generation or projectivity of the $Q_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, initial, limit and least-missing-element recursion and exhaustion paragraphs, abstracting only the successor property (old proof steps 1, 3, 4 and 8)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem] well-order the set of all pairs of a submodule of $M$ and a subset of $I$. Choose, once for each pair $(U,H)$ satisfying $T(U)=D_H$ and $U\ne M$, the least witness $(V,H')$ to the assumed successor property for the least $x\in M\setminus U$. The witness set is nonempty by hypothesis; the fixed well-order makes this a specified rule. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] to $E=\{\alpha:\alpha\leq\kappa\}$, with values pairs of a submodule of $M$ and a subset of $I$. At zero put $(0,\varnothing)$. At a successor apply the selected witness if the preceding pair is valid and its module is not $M$; otherwise keep that pair. At a nonzero limit take the unions of preceding modules and subsets if the preceding modules form an increasing family, and put $(0,\varnothing)$ otherwise. An increasing union is a submodule: two members lie together in the larger of their stages, where their sum and scalar multiples lie. Thus the rule is defined for every possible preceding family, as the recursion node requires. The subsequent steps prove that only the valid branches occur.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, proof: initial stage, limit union, least-missing-element successor and exhaustion paragraphs; successor enlargement is assumed here

proof.text: The recursive families are increasing, independently of the coordinate invariant. Indeed a successor always contains its predecessor: this is part of a selected witness, and is an equality on the other branch. If increasingness first failed at a nonzero limit, all earlier stages would form a chain, so the rule at that limit would take their union and contain each earlier stage, a contradiction. At a successor the same conclusion follows from containment of its predecessor and the earlier chain. There is no failure at zero. Consequently the union branch always applies, giving both required continuity identities at every nonzero limit.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, proof: initial stage, limit union, least-missing-element successor and exhaustion paragraphs; successor enlargement is assumed here

proof.text: We prove $T(M_\alpha)=D_{H_\alpha}$ by induction on $\alpha$. At zero every pure tensor in $B\otimes_A0$ is zero, by bilinearity, and pure tensors generate the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $T(0)=0$. The only family vanishing outside $\varnothing$ is the zero family [def-trf-coordinate-submodule], so $T(M_0)=D_{H_0}$. At a successor, if the preceding module is proper, the induction hypothesis makes its pair valid and the selected witness gives $T(M_{\alpha+1})=D_{H_{\alpha+1}}$ as well as containment of the least missing element. If the preceding module is $M$, the rule is stationary, so the same coordinate equality persists.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, proof: initial stage, limit union, least-missing-element successor and exhaustion paragraphs; successor enlargement is assumed here

proof.text: For the limit step let $0<\lambda\leq\kappa$ be a limit, with the coordinate equality known for every $\alpha<\lambda$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], an element of $B\otimes_A M_\lambda$ is a finite sum $\sum_j b_j\otimes m_j$. Each $m_j$ lies in an earlier $M_{\alpha_j}$; choose the maximum of these finitely many indices, or $0<\lambda$ if the sum is empty. The sum is then the image of a tensor over that stage. Conversely inclusion $M_\alpha\subseteq M_\lambda$ gives a factorization of the inclusion-induced tensor maps, by their pure-tensor formula and uniqueness. Applying $\theta$ proves $T(M_\lambda)=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}T(M_\alpha)$. Similarly, an element of $D_{H_\lambda}$ has finite support in $\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}H_\alpha$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule] [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Choose a stage for each support index and take their finite maximum, or stage zero for empty support. It lies in that stage's $D_{H_\alpha}$. The reverse inclusion follows from $H_\alpha\subseteq H_\lambda$. Hence $D_{H_\lambda}=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}D_{H_\alpha}=T(M_\lambda)$. This completes the induction; in particular the invalid successor branch never occurs.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, proof: initial stage, limit union, least-missing-element successor and exhaustion paragraphs; successor enlargement is assumed here

proof.text: At every nonstationary successor the chosen witness states directly that $M_{\alpha+1}/M_\alpha$ is countably generated and projective; these are assumptions of the enlargement property, not consequences of flatness. At a stationary successor this quotient has just the zero coset by [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. It is generated by the empty set. It is projective by the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]: every map from this zero module is zero and lifts along any surjection by the zero map. This proves the quotient assertion in both branches.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, proof: initial stage, limit union, least-missing-element successor and exhaustion paragraphs; successor enlargement is assumed here

proof.text: Finally induct on $\alpha\leq\kappa$ to show $e_\beta\in M_\alpha$ for all $\beta<\alpha$. At zero there is nothing to check. At $\alpha+1$, all $e_\beta$ with $\beta<\alpha$ persist by increasingness. If $e_\alpha$ is already present, it too persists. Otherwise every earlier element in the fixed well-order is present by induction, so $e_\alpha$ is exactly the least missing element and is added by the nonstationary successor. At a nonzero limit $\lambda$, for $\beta<\lambda$ one has $\beta+1<\lambda$, so $e_\beta\in M_{\beta+1}\subseteq M_\lambda$. Surjectivity of the enumeration gives $M_\kappa=M$. These inductions can equivalently be read as least-counterexample arguments in the specified ordinal well-order. The recursion and the preceding steps give every asserted identity and successor condition. Only finite tensor expressions and finite coordinate supports were used; no injectivity after tensoring, flatness, or generation or projectivity of any $Q_i$ was used.
